title: A trip for two
titleJp: {二人|ふたり}で{旅行|りょこう}

canDos.text: Plan a short trip: say where you plan to go, how long you'll stay and what you want to see.

check.instructions: Your partner (or the AI) asks you the three questions below about a trip you'd like to take. Answer each one in one or two sentences of casual Japanese, without notes.
check.material:
{今度|こんど}の{休|やす}み、どこに{行|い}くつもり？
{何日|なんにち}ぐらい{行|い}くの？どこに{泊|と}まる？
{何|なに}をするつもり？{何|なに}が{見|み}たい？
rubric: Names a place and says it is the plan with 〜つもり (きょうとに いく つもり)
Says how long they will stay and where (ふたばん とまる, りょかんに とまる)
Gives at least two things to see or do (〜たり〜たり, or 〜と〜)
Gives a reason at least once with ので or から

canDos.text: Read a ryokan or hotel information sheet (check-in time, meals, bath hours) and answer questions about it.

check.instructions: You're staying at this ryokan tonight. Read its information sheet, then answer the questions.
check.material:
{旅館|りょかん}「さくら」のご{案内|あんない}
お{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}る{時間|じかん}　15:00〜19:00
お{部屋|へや}を{出|で}る{時間|じかん}　〜10:00
{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}　18:00〜20:00（お{部屋|へや}で）
{朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}　7:30〜9:00（{食堂|しょくどう}で）
{温泉|おんせん}　15:00〜24:00／{朝|あさ} 6:00〜9:00
※{夜|よる}12{時|じ}から{朝|あさ}6{時|じ}までは、{温泉|おんせん}に{入|はい}らないでください。
※タオルはお{部屋|へや}にあります。{温泉|おんせん}に{持|も}っていってください。
※{駅|えき}まで{無料|むりょう}のバスがあります（10:00・14:00・16:00）。

questions.q: What time can you check in?

options: At a restaurant near the station

questions.q: You want a bath at 1:00 a.m. What does the sheet say?
options: Fine: the bath is open all night
Don't use the hot spring between midnight and 6:00 a.m.
Ask for a towel at the front desk first

canDos.text: Understand a friend's travel tips and what they've heard about a place (the food's great, it's crowded in autumn).

check.instructions: Your friend Yuki left you a voice message about Kyoto. Listen (you can play it twice), then answer the questions.
check.material:
もしもし、ゆきです。{京都|きょうと}に{行|い}くんだって？いいね！
{私|わたし}は{去年|きょねん}の{秋|あき}に{行|い}ったけど、{人|ひと}が{多|おお}くて{大変|たいへん}だったよ。
{冬|ふゆ}は{寒|さむ}いけど、{人|ひと}は{少|すく}ないよ。
{友達|ともだち}は、{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くの{豆腐|とうふ}{料理|りょうり}の{店|みせ}がとてもおいしいって{言|い}ってた。
あと、{昼|ひる}は{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いので、お{寺|てら}は{朝|あさ}{行|い}ったほうがいいって。
じゃあ、{楽|たの}しんでね！お{土産|みやげ}、よろしく！

questions.q: What did Yuki find hard about Kyoto in autumn?

options: A tofu restaurant near the station
A hot spring outside the city
A ramen shop by a temple

questions.q: When does Yuki say you should visit the temples, and why?
options: In the evening, because they're lit up
At lunchtime, because the trains are empty
In the morning, because it's crowded during the day

canDos.text: Explain politely why you need something at a hotel or station, and make a request ('It's our first time here, so…').

check.instructions: You've just arrived at a ryokan. The AI (or your partner) plays the clerk and says the three lines below. Answer each politely in です/ます: explain your situation with ので, then make a request. 1) You're early and want to leave your bags. 2) It's your first time in this town, so you'd like a map or some tips. 3) You'll be back late from sightseeing, so you'd like dinner later.
check.material:
いらっしゃいませ。すみません、お{部屋|へや}は{三時|さんじ}からなんです。
はい。ほかに{何|なに}かありますか。
{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}は{六時|ろくじ}からですが、{何時|なんじ}がいいですか。
rubric: Gives a reason with ので in each answer (これから まちを みに いくので…, はじめてなので…)
Makes a clear request: 〜てもいいですか, 〜てください or 〜を おねがいします
Keeps to です/ます throughout, with no casual forms
Names a specific time for dinner (しちじはんに おねがいします)

canDos.text: Write a postcard-style message about your trip: where you went, what was great and what wasn't.

check.instructions: Your friend sent the message below. Reply in 4–6 sentences about a trip you've taken (real or made up): where you went and for how long, one thing that was great and one that wasn't. Use は to contrast the two.
check.material: お{帰|かえ}り！{旅行|りょこう}、どうだった？どこに{泊|と}まったの？{写真|しゃしん}{見|み}せて！
rubric: Says where they went and how long they stayed
Contrasts a good point and a bad point with は (りょかんは よかったけど、てんきは…)
Uses past forms correctly (〜た / 〜かった, or 〜ました / 〜かったです)
Uses だけ or しか〜ない at least once (ひとばん だけ, ふつか しか いなかった)

task.goal: Plan a two-night trip: share what you each know about two places and agree where to go, how to get there and where to stay.
task.outcomeQuestion: Where are you going, how are you getting there, where are you staying, and what is the total for the two of you?

roles.a: Has the guide page for a hot-spring town (card A)
roles.b: Has the guide page for a seaside town and your budget (card B)

task.infoA: Card A: the hot-spring town (おんせんの まち). Shinkansen (しんかんせん) 2 hours, then a 30-minute bus. Train fare ¥14,000 per person, there and back. Ryokan (りょかん) with an outdoor bath, dinner and breakfast: ¥18,000 per person per night. Business hotel by the station: ¥7,000 per person per night, no meals. Famous for hot springs, mountain walks and soba (そば). A friend says it's a quiet, laid-back town (しずかで のんびりした まちだって), but there's nothing to do at night. You'd love at least one night in the ryokan.
task.infoB: Card B: the seaside town (うみの まち). Local train (でんしゃ) 3 hours, no changes. Train fare ¥8,000 per person, there and back. Small hotel by the sea (うみの ちかくの ホテル): ¥9,000 per person per night, breakfast included. Famous for sashimi (さしみ) and boat trips (ふね). Your budget: ¥60,000 in total for the two of you, trains and rooms (ぜんぶで ろくまんえん しか ない). Two nights, leaving Friday. You'd love to eat fresh fish.
task.twist: Same two towns, but now one of you can only take one day off, so it is a one-night trip, and the budget drops to ¥35,000 (さんまん ごせんえん). Which town still works? Re-plan and agree again.

scripted.jp: ねえ、{温泉|おんせん}の{町|まち}と{海|うみ}の{町|まち}、どっちに{行|い}きたい？
scripted.en: Hey, the hot-spring town or the seaside town: which one do you want to go to?

scripted.jp: {海|うみ}かな。{刺身|さしみ}がとてもおいしいって。{温泉|おんせん}の{町|まち}は？
scripted.en: The sea, I think. They say the sashimi's really good. What's the hot-spring town like?

scripted.jp: {静|しず}かで、のんびりした{町|まち}だって。{夜|よる}は{何|なに}もないけど。
scripted.en: Apparently it's a quiet, laid-back town. There's nothing to do at night, though.

scripted.jp: {新幹線|しんかんせん}で{二時間|にじかん}。でも、{電車|でんしゃ}だけで{二人|ふたり}で{二万八千円|にまんはっせんえん}かかるよ。
scripted.en: Two hours on the shinkansen. But the trains alone come to ¥28,000 for the two of us.

scripted.jp: {海|うみ}は{三時間|さんじかん}かかるけど、{二人|ふたり}で{一万六千円|いちまんろくせんえん}だよ。
scripted.en: The sea takes three hours, but it's ¥16,000 for both of us.

scripted.jp: {旅館|りょかん}に{泊|と}まりたいな。{一人|ひとり}{一万八千円|いちまんはっせんえん}だけど…。
scripted.en: I'd love to stay at the ryokan. It's ¥18,000 each, though…

scripted.jp: お{金|かね}は{全部|ぜんぶ}で{六万円|ろくまんえん}しかないので、{旅館|りょかん}は{無理|むり}だね。
scripted.en: We've only got ¥60,000 in total, so the ryokan's out.

scripted.jp: そっか。じゃあ、{温泉|おんせん}はまた{今度|こんど}にしよう。{海|うみ}のホテルはいくら？
scripted.en: I see. Then let's save the hot spring for another time. How much is the hotel by the sea?

scripted.jp: {一人|ひとり}{九千円|きゅうせんえん}で、{朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}もあるよ。{二晩|ふたばん}{泊|と}まって、{全部|ぜんぶ}で{五万二千円|ごまんにせんえん}。
scripted.en: ¥9,000 each, with breakfast. Two nights, and it's ¥52,000 altogether.

scripted.jp: いいね。じゃあ、{海|うみ}にしよう！いつ{行|い}く？
scripted.en: Great. Let's go to the sea, then! When shall we go?

scripted.jp: {金曜日|きんようび}に{行|い}って、{日曜日|にちようび}に{帰|かえ}るつもり。{八千円|はっせんえん}は、おいしい{魚|さかな}に{使|つか}おう！
scripted.en: I'm thinking we go on Friday and come back on Sunday. And let's spend the other ¥8,000 on good fish!

capstone.title: Our trip
capstone.brief: Act out a trip from planning to coming home: decide where you plan to go and for how long, pass on what friends said about it, check in politely at a ryokan with a request, and on the way home talk about what was great and what wasn't.
